rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient to observe all 10 compounds while retaining early eluters and allowing time for strongly retained compounds to elute. The retention and resolution pattern will guide subsequent optimization of gradient range, duration, and temperature.

Halve the gradient duration to reduce the last-peak time while testing how much of the current resolution margin can be traded for speed. Keep temperature and solvent endpoints fixed to isolate the effect of gradient steepness.

Test whether higher temperature separates the crowded middle peaks while preserving the short run time. Keeping the gradient unchanged isolates temperature-dependent selectivity as a route to improving resolution without a time penalty.

Probe intermediate-temperature selectivity to seek a window between the middle-peak crowding at 40 °C and the near-coelution at 60 °C. The unchanged fast gradient should keep the time penalty at zero.

Test 55 °C to improve the remaining close pair at 50 °C while checking whether the pair that nearly coelutes at 60 °C remains adequately separated. The last-peak time should remain within the zero-penalty region.

Slightly lengthen the gradient at the best temperature to improve the remaining under-resolved pair, while monitoring the other close pair for selectivity changes. The last peak is expected to remain near the zero-time-penalty region.

Test a slightly shallower gradient near the maximum-scoring method by lowering the final organic fraction. This may improve the resolution margin of the earlier close pair while keeping the last peak near the zero-time-penalty window; the later close pair will be monitored for any loss of resolution.

Test a modestly higher starting organic fraction to shorten retention while probing selectivity around the two close pairs. The maximum CRF is already achieved; this distinct neighboring method tests whether that score can be retained with a shorter last-peak time.

Lower the final organic fraction to recover resolution of the close pair in injection 8 while retaining its higher starting fraction. This slightly shallower gradient may achieve full resolution with no time penalty and a better minimum-resolution margin than injection 6.

Further reduce gradient steepness to lift the remaining close pair above R = 1.5 while preserving separation of the other critical pair. Extrapolation from injections 8–9 places the last peak near 8 minutes, potentially retaining zero time penalty.

Preserve injection 6’s gradient slope and temperature while ending the ramp earlier at a lower organic fraction. Because all peaks previously eluted before this new ramp ends, this method should retain CRF 1.000 without requiring the 0.95 endpoint.

Use a gradient slope between injections 9 and 10 to target full resolution with a last-peak time below 8 minutes. This may retain the maximum CRF while balancing resolution margin against the onset of the time penalty.

Keep the maximum-scoring gradient slope and temperature while testing a lower endpoint and shorter ramp. The gradient reaches its endpoint at the outlet at 8.65 minutes, after the previous last peak at 7.60 minutes, so the observed separation should remain unchanged.

Test a higher starting organic fraction with a compensating shallower gradient to seek another fully resolved, zero-penalty method. This probes whether the improved separation of the later critical pair can be retained without sacrificing the earlier pair or delaying the last peak beyond 8 minutes.

Explore lower-temperature selectivity with the fast scouting gradient to look for a separate maximum-score region. Cooling may resolve the middle-peak cluster through a different elution pattern, although the last-peak time must be checked for a time penalty.

Retain the maximum-scoring gradient slope through the first nine peaks, then test whether a hold at 0.50 organic elutes the last compound before the time penalty begins. This explores a lower-endpoint alternative while preserving the established critical-pair separation.

Test a slightly shallower gradient than injection 10 to increase the earlier critical pair’s resolution while monitoring the later pair. Injection 16 demonstrates that 8.35 minutes still incurs no time penalty, leaving room to seek a larger resolution margin at the maximum CRF.

Use a shallower gradient to recover the earlier critical pair’s resolution at the higher starting organic fraction tested in injection 14. This may provide a larger minimum-resolution margin while retaining the maximum CRF, although the later elution time must be checked for a penalty.

Preserve injection 10’s gradient slope and temperature while lowering the endpoint to 0.60 organic. The outlet ramp ends at 8.65 minutes, after its last peak at 8.00 minutes, so this distinct method should retain CRF 1.000 and the same resolution margins.

Test higher-temperature selectivity with a ramp followed by a moderate-organic hold, which may separate the earlier critical pair after an elution-order reversal. The maximum score is already secured; this explores a distinct route to full resolution with a short run.

Return to 55 °C and slightly flatten injection 17’s gradient to test the slower edge of the maximum-score region. The earlier critical pair should gain resolution, while the later pair and last-peak time will determine whether CRF 1.000 is retained.

Test a lower-endpoint method with a slope close to injection 21, which achieved the maximum CRF. The critical pairs should elute during the ramp with similar resolution, while the final hold tests whether the last compound still elutes without a time penalty.

Test an intermediate gradient slope between maximum-scoring injections 17 and 21. Both critical pairs are expected to remain above R = 1.5, with the last peak within the demonstrated zero-penalty window.

Test a 5 °C decrease from maximum-scoring injection 11 to assess temperature sensitivity at the established gradient slope. This will show whether full resolution persists at a neighboring temperature rather than only at 55 °C.

Return to 55 °C and test a gradient slope between injections 8 and 9 to refine the fast boundary of the full-resolution region. The maximum CRF is already secured; this final run checks whether a shorter method can retain it.
